subject: Onboarding: Account blueprint + DNS & Firewall signoffs (Novacare)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@novacare.com>, Ops Team <ops@novacare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: Account blueprint + DNS & Firewall signoffs (Novacare)

Hi Aisha / Novacare ops team —

Thanks for the kickoff call this morning. Per our agreement, attached is the account "blueprint" and a compact DNS & firewall signoff template to speed the final validation. Please review the checklist below and confirm by EOD Tuesday if Novacare can sign off on network controls so we can schedule the environment provisioning window.

Quick checklist (high impact items):
- CIDR allocation and subnet mapping: confirm the /20 assigned for Redwood-hosted enclave and the two /24s we discussed for management and workload planes.
- DNS records: authoritative A/CNAME for service endpoints, internal split-horizon entries for private endpoints, and PTR for any static egress IPs.
- Firewall rules: inbound allowed ports (443 for control plane & API, 22 restricted to bastion IP; 10250 between control plane and nodes if using kube; NTP 123 to company NTP pool).
- Egress NAT: provide the static public IPs or NAT range we should expect for outbound telemetry and control plane callbacks.
- Service accounts & IAM: KMS principal email + required roles for key unwrap and audit logging.
- Bastion access: bastion jump host FQDN, allowed SSH source CIDRs, and privileged access window process.
- TLS & certs: mutual TLS expectation — do you want us to generate SANs or will you provide cert chain?
- Audit & retention: log destination and minimum retention (we default to 90 days unless otherwise specified).

Attachments: redwood-onboard-account-blueprint-v1.xlsx (account mapping + sample subnet plan), dns-firewall-signoff-template.pdf (fillable signoff), novacare-macros-access-list.csv (fields we need filled).

Next steps: if you can populate the signoff PDF and return it with any amended firewall rules, we will queue the provisioning and reserve the day for smoke tests. If there are any blockers (eg compliance needs for inbound inspection or mandatory proxying), flag them here and we'll loop in our security lead.

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Onboarding, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

---
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@novacare.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@novacare.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Account blueprint + DNS & Firewall signoffs (Novacare)

Thanks Marcus — we've taken a first pass and have three clarifying questions before we sign: 

1) Split-horizon DNS: Novacare runs internal authoritative for our corp zone (novacare.local). For private endpoints, do you require us to create internal-only A records (split-horizon) pointing at the private IPs you will provision, or do you accept using private hostnames under the redwood-managed zone (we prefer to keep control in-house)?

2) Reverse PTR for egress IPs: our SOC wants PTR entries for any static public IPs used by your egress — do you have a process for providing PTRs or should we provide the delegation ticket?

3) MTU & fragmentation: our network team saw recommendations for jumbo frames in some Redwood docs. We cannot enable jumbo frames across our VPCs; what's the safe MTU you recommend (we assume 1500).

Also, attached is our internal firewall config export for the expected perimeter changes (novacare-fw-export-20270502.json). We will not be able to open broad outbound 0.0.0.0/0 to any destination other than the listed Redwood telemetry endpoints — can you provide a minimal egress list (hostnames + IPs) you will call out?

We aim to return the filled signoff by tomorrow if the above items are resolved.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Infrastructure — Novacare Health
aisha.rahman@novacare.com

---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@novacare.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Account blueprint + DNS & Firewall signoffs (Novacare)

Hi Aisha — quick answers from the infra side (Kimberly / Marcus, feel free to add):

1) Split-horizon DNS: we can support either model. If Novacare wants to keep authoritative control, please create internal-only A records for the 3 private endpoints (management, runtime, bastion) and map them to the private IPs we'll hand over once the host provisioning completes. If you'd rather we manage hostnames under redwood-internal.redwood.com, we'll provide delegated zone NS and a short TTL plan. We prefer the first option for customers with strict DNS policies.

2) PTR/delegation: we can provide the list of static egress IPs and the expected PTR strings. If you prefer to file the PTR delegation ticket, we'll supply the reverse delegation block and the canonical names to be used.

3) MTU: 1500 is the recommended safe baseline for hybrid connectivity. We'll avoid jumbo frames.

Minimal egress endpoints (short list):
- control.redwood-internal.net:443 (control plane callbacks and orchestration)
- telemetry.redwood-internal.net:443 (metrics/agent telemetry)
- crl.redwood-internal.net:443 (CRL/OCSP checks)
- container-registry.redwood-internal.net:443 (image pulls during provisioning)

We will provide a one-page IP/hostname table in the final signoff PDF, but please plan to allow outbound 443 to the above hostnames; if your firewall requires IPs, we'll publish the IP set in the signoff doc (note: IPs may be updated; we use small stable ranges and post-change notice).

Service account / IAM notes:
- KMS: create a key policy granting the principal redwood-service@redwood.com the Decrypt and DescribeKey permissions. We will not keep unencrypted secrets.
- Audit logs: grant write to the logging sink service account (sink@novacare-logs.iam.gserviceaccount.com) for the redwood logging prefix.

Bastion: restrict 22 to the 2 IP ranges listed in novacare-macros-access-list.csv. We'll use ephemeral certs for session access; public key install will be coordinated during provisioning.

If that all looks reasonable, Marcus can mark this as "ready for provisioning" and we will allocate the slot.

Thanks
Ben Carter
Engineering Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: 2027-05-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Account blueprint + DNS & Firewall signoffs (Novacare)

Marcus / Ben / Kimberly —

Quick update: we've completed the internal changes requested.

- Split-horizon DNS: internal A records created for management.novacare.local, runtime.novacare.local, bastion.novacare.local (internal-only, TTL 300).
- PTR: delegation request filed with our netops team; we'll share the ticket ID during provisioning.
- MTU: confirmed baseline 1500 across connectors.
- Firewall: perimeter rules updated to allow outbound HTTPS to the hostnames you provided; we will accept your IP published list once you attach it to the signoff PDF.
- KMS / IAM: created key novacare-redwood-onboard and granted Decrypt to redwood-service@redwood.com.

Attached: novacare_signed_firewall_signoff.pdf (fillable signoff completed). We also included the novacare-fw-changes-20270503.diff for your reference.

Please confirm you have what you need to proceed with provisioning and give an ETA for the smoke window. Prefer to run smoke on Thursday morning PT.

Thanks —
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Director, Infrastructure — Novacare Health
